subject: [PATCH v2 2/5] btrfs: split btrfs_insert_delayed_dir_index() into prealloc and commit phases

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested simplifying the btrfs_prealloc_delayed_dir_index() function by returning a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer instead of taking it as an argument, reducing the parameter list.
reviews.raw_body:
We can directly return a btrfs_dir_index_prealloc pointer, which reduce 
the parameter list.

Otherwise looks good to me.

Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>

Thanks,
Qu

2026-08-05.patch_summary: This patch splits the btrfs_insert_delayed_dir_index() function into three separate functions: prealloc, commit, and free. The prealloc function allocates memory for a delayed node and item before modifying the B-tree, allowing -ENOMEM to be returned cleanly if allocation fails. The commit function populates the item data and inserts it into the rb-tree, while the free function releases pre-allocated resources in case of failure. This refactoring improves error handling and reduces the risk of aborting transactions due to memory allocation failures.
